[WP] A day in the life of a lone robot on an abandoned Earth.

A shooting star shot past the heavens.

It watched, silent and motionless, as the star burnt its mark into the empty skies.

In its blazing dance, not even the moon or the stars could compete with its glory.

Yet, its beauty is brief. That fiery dance could end in nothing but its own eventual destruction.

As if in response to that thought, the meteor disappeared behind a cloud and didn't reappear again.

It turned its eyes back towards the road. Long ago, its creators had told many stories about the shooting star. That it was the sign of a fallen angel. That it was a messenger of the gods, and that a wish made upon a shooting star would reach the ears of the gods themselves. That it was a golden tear from the god of stone who sad alone on his iron throne. All sorts of different and wonderful stories.

To it, however, the shooting star was just a shooting star.

The humans, and their stories, were long gone.

Long ago, father had sat by the river, and told it many things. Some of them were useful - most of them were annoying.

It didn't like the stories back then. The stories confused it and made it angry. How could the river gods exist, when rivers were made of nothing but water? How could a mountain be torn asunder by the grief of a god that was not? The stories were annoying, particularly because of all their inconsistencies.

Father had simply laughed its worries aside. You'd understand someday. Sometimes, the right answer isn't as important as the beautiful answer.

This was a joint trial between the University of Nottingham and Texas Tech University

Initial lab tests showed the concoction killed staph, while its individual ingredients, tested separately, did not. They turned to Kendra Rumbaugh, PhD, whose lab at Texas Tech University’s Health Sciences Center frequently conducts efficacy studies of new antimicrobial compounds. She tested it using lab mice, by creating a surgical incision, infecting it with staph, killing the mice and harvesting the tissue, and then soaking the infected tissue in the medieval concoction as well as a vancomycin solution and plain saline. In the tissue treated with the medieval compound, 90 percent of the staph died.
